description_full: Yamato Kogyo Co., Ltd., through its subsidiaries, engages in the manufacture and sale of steel products in Japan and internationally. The company offers H-beam, channel steel, I-beam, equal angle, steel sheet pile, rolled steel for shipbuilding, bent and cast steel products. It also provides trackwork materials, such as turnouts, anti-derailing/deviation guards, expansion joints, NEW crossings, adhesive insulated joint rails, tie plates, and bolts. In addition, it offers jumbo H-beams, Z sheet piles, angles, and rebars. Further, it is involved in the transportation and medical waste treatment, as well as produces counterweight products. The company was incorporated in 1944 and is headquartered in Himeji, Japan.

financial_summary: YAMATO KOGYO CO is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $3.0B market cap on $1.0B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -7% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -2.2pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.

Returns on capital run at 3% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 18% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $254M in free cash flow — roughly 25 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.83× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 22× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 10.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 39% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
